title: BGP & Anycast
summary: BGP is how autonomous systems exchange reachability. Anycast announces the same prefix from many locations so users hit a nearby PoP. Together they power CDNs, DNS, and DDoS absorption — and create failure modes that look like 'random' routing flaps.

sections.title: Autonomous systems and BGP basics
paragraphs: The internet is a network of Autonomous Systems (AS). BGP advertises prefixes with AS paths. Policy — not pure shortest path — decides what you accept and export. That policy surface is why a single misconfiguration can blackhole traffic globally.
iBGP distributes routes inside an AS; eBGP speaks between ASes. Route reflectors and confederations scale iBGP. Attributes like LOCAL_PREF, MED, and AS path length influence selection.
For system designers, BGP matters when you run multi-homed services, anycast edges, or need to understand why traffic suddenly shifts regions.

sections.title: Anycast as a design tool
paragraphs: Anycast means many servers advertise the same IP prefix. Routers deliver packets to the 'nearest' announcement by routing metrics. DNS resolvers and CDN edges use this so clients land on a nearby PoP without an application-level directory.

Anycast is great for request/response UDP/TCP services that tolerate connection resets on route change. It is a poor fit for long-lived connections that must pin to one backend unless you terminate quickly at the PoP.
Health withdrawal is critical: if a PoP is sick but still announces, it becomes a blackhole. Couple BGP announcements with health-checked control planes.

sections.title: Failures and operational controls
paragraphs: Route leaks, hijacks, and RPKI invalid announcements are real. Monitoring control-plane (BMP, looking glasses) matters as much as data-plane latency.
Traffic engineering uses prepends, communities, and selective announcements. Overuse creates brittle topologies that break during maintenance.

sections.title: Design implications
paragraphs: When designing a global API, decide whether geo-DNS, anycast, or client-side region selection owns steering. Mixing all three without a clear source of truth causes oscillation.
State replication must match steering: if users flip PoPs, sticky server state will orphan sessions unless state is global or PoP-local with sticky routing.

deepDive.title: BGP & Anycast — Operations
paragraphs: Operating BGP & Anycast in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: BGP & Anycast — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around BGP & Anycast include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: BGP & Anycast — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, BGP & Anycast intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Withdraw anycast on PoP health failure quickly
Monitor control plane and data plane separately
Prefer simple steering policies you can explain in an incident

examples.description: Anycast VIP in front of regional caches.

keyTakeaways: BGP is policy-driven reachability between ASes
Anycast steers users to nearby healthy announcements
Steering and state placement must be designed together
whyItMatters: Global systems fail in routing-shaped ways. If you cannot reason about BGP and anycast, you cannot design multi-region edges safely.
reflectionQuestions: When would you prefer geo-DNS over anycast?
What happens to TCP connections when anycast routes shift mid-flow?
numbersToKnow: BGP convergence: seconds to minutes depending on failure
Anycast: best for short connections / edge termination
